review.tagline: Companion notebooks for the O'Reilly book Hands-On Large Language Models
review.summary: Code for every example in the book by Jay Alammar and Maarten Grootendorst, as one Jupyter notebook per chapter. Chapters cover tokens and embeddings, transformer internals, classification, clustering, prompt engineering, semantic search and RAG, multimodal models, and fine-tuning. Notebooks were built and tested on Google Colab with a free 16GB T4 GPU.
review.audience: Developers learning how LLMs work who want runnable chapter code
strengths: One notebook per chapter (12), each with an Open in Colab link
Covers embeddings, RAG, multimodal models and fine-tuning of BERT and generation models
Tested mainly on free Colab T4 16GB, so no local GPU is required
Bonus folder links to visual guides on Mamba, quantization and mixture of experts
weaknesses: Explanatory text and figures are in the paid book, not in the repo
Local setup is only a quick-start guide; results may differ by OS and versions
No tagged releases; README states no pinned package versions
Not a library or tool, only teaching code
